method_card.title: Gaming and Digital Entertainment
method_card.content:
This lesson covers video games, online gaming and digital habits. Key grammar: desde hace + present for ongoing duration, time markers, and comparatives.

SpanishEnglish
el videojuegovideo game
la consolagames console
jugar en líneato play online
el juego en líneaonline game
el ordenadorcomputer
la tabletatablet
los juegos de aventuraadventure games
los juegos de estrategiastrategy games
los juegos de deportessports games
jugar con amigos en líneato play with friends online
pasar tiempoto spend time
al día / a la semanaper day / per week
desde hace + timefor (ongoing duration)
el control parentalparental controls
la adicción / la dependenciaaddiction / dependence (Higher)

Grammar focus — desde hace + present: To say how long you have been doing something (and you are still doing it), use: verb (present tense) + desde hace + time expression. Example: Juego a videojuegos desde hace tres años. (I have been playing video games for three years.) Do NOT use the perfect tense here — that is an English habit that Spanish does not share.

Time markers: todos los días (every day), a veces (sometimes), de vez en cuando (from time to time), durante + time (for — duration of a completed period), desde hace + time (for — ongoing to now).

Model paragraph: Juego a videojuegos desde hace dos años. Prefiero los juegos de aventura porque son más emocionantes que los juegos de deportes. Suelo jugar en línea con mis amigos los fines de semana durante dos horas. (I have been playing video games for two years. I prefer adventure games because they are more exciting than sports games. I usually play online with my friends at weekends for two hours.)
steps: Learn the key vocabulary for video games, consoles and digital habits
Master desde hace + present tense for ongoing duration
Practise time markers: todos los días, a veces, durante, desde hace
Build extended sentences with comparatives and connectives

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — gaming and digital life appear across all papers in Theme 4

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: Juego a videojuegos desde hace dos años.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Juego = I play (present tense). a videojuegos = video games (note: jugar a — you need a after jugar).

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: desde hace dos años = for two years (ongoing, up to now). Spanish uses the present tense here; English uses 'I have been playing'.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: I have been playing video games for two years.

worked_examples.question: Spot the difference: why is 'He jugado a videojuegos desde hace tres años' incorrect?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: He jugado is the perfect tense (I have played). In Spanish, desde hace is always used with the present tense, not the perfect.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: The perfect tense implies a completed action. Desde hace expresses an ongoing action (still happening now), so the present is correct.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: The correct sentence is: Juego a videojuegos desde hace tres años.

bronze.question: Match the Spanish gaming vocabulary to its English meaning
Match the Spanish time expressions and phrases to their English meaning
Complete the sentence
sentence_parts: los juegos de aventura porque son emocionantes.

gaps.rule: desde hace — fixed phrase for ongoing duration
gaps.correct_explain: desde hace is a fixed phrase meaning 'for (up to now)'. Always use the present tense of the verb before it.

wrong.que: desde que means 'since (a point in time)', not 'for (a duration)'. Use desde hace + time expression.
wrong.tiempo: desde tiempo is not a standard phrase. The correct structure is desde hace + number + time unit.

gaps.correct_explain: Prefiero means 'I prefer'. It is a stem-changing verb: prefiero, prefieres, prefiere.

wrong.Prefiere: Prefiere is the él/ella form. First person singular = prefiero.
wrong.Gusto: Gusto is not how this works. Use me gusta (with indirect object pronoun) or simply prefiero (I prefer).

bronze.question: Complete the sentence
sentence_parts: en línea con mis amigos los fines de semana

gaps.correct_explain: Suelo jugar means 'I usually play'. After soler, always use the infinitive.

wrong.juego: juego is the conjugated form. After suelo, use the infinitive: jugar.
wrong.jugando: jugando is the gerund. After soler, use the infinitive: jugar.

gaps.correct_explain: durante means 'for' when referring to a completed or bounded period of time (two hours of gaming this session).

wrong.desde hace: desde hace expresses ongoing duration up to now (e.g. for three years). durante is better for 'two hours of gaming tonight'.

bronze.question: What does 'Juego a videojuegos desde hace cuatro años' mean?
options: I have been playing video games for four years
I played video games four years ago
I started playing video games in four years
I used to play video games four years ago

bronze.question: What does 'Prefiero los juegos de estrategia porque son más interesantes que los juegos de deportes' mean?
options: I prefer strategy games because they are more interesting than sports games
I like sports games because they are more interesting than strategy games
Strategy games are less interesting than sports games
I find sports games and strategy games equally interesting

bronze.source_text: Juego en línea con mis amigos todos los días durante una hora.
model_answers: I play online with my friends every day for an hour.
hints: jugar en línea = to play online

silver.question: Complete the sentence
sentence_parts: Juego en línea desde hace cinco años y
que es una buena manera de pasar el tiempo, aunque

gaps.correct_explain: creo (I think/believe) is the first person present of creer. pienso and opino are also correct.

wrong.cree: cree is the él/ella form. The subject is 'I' → creo.

gaps.correct_explain: puede (it can) is the third person singular present of poder. Here the implied subject is 'it' (gaming) — no subject pronoun needed.

wrong.puedo: puedo is first person (I can). The subject here is 'it' (gaming) → puede.
wrong.podría: podría is conditional (it could). Present tense is more direct: puede.

silver.english: I have been playing online for five years and I **think** it is a good way to spend time, although it **can** be addictive.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: He jugado a videojuegos desde hace tres años.
silver.error_type: Tense — desde hace requires present, not perfect
silver.explanation: In Spanish, desde hace (for — ongoing) always takes the present tense. He jugado is the perfect tense — correct in English ('I have been playing') but wrong in Spanish. Use Juego a videojuegos desde hace tres años.
silver.translation: I have been playing video games for three years.

silver.question: Build the sentence in Spanish
silver.english: Adventure games are more exciting than strategy games.

distractor_labels.muy: wrong word — very is muy, but 'more' in a comparison is más. Structure: más + adjective + que.

silver.source_text: I have been playing online games for three years and I usually play for two hours per day.
model_answers: Juego a juegos en línea desde hace tres años y suelo jugar durante dos horas al día.
hints: I have been playing = juego (present) + desde hace
for two hours = durante dos horas

gold.source_text: I have been playing video games for five years. I prefer online games because they are more entertaining than offline games. However, I think it is important to control how much time you spend gaming each day.
model_answers: Juego a videojuegos desde hace cinco años. Prefiero los juegos en línea porque son más entretenidos que los juegos sin conexión. Sin embargo, creo que es importante controlar cuánto tiempo pasas jugando cada día.

gold.question: Build the sentence in Spanish
gold.english: I think that online gaming is more interesting than watching TV, but it can be more addictive.

distractor_labels.interesante: wrong number — juegos is plural, so the adjective must be plural: interesantes
distractor_labels.son más: duplicate — más is already in the sentence; do not repeat it

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are at a leisure centre in Spain. You speak to the receptionist about the gaming tournament they are hosting this weekend.

bullets.prompt: Greet the receptionist and ask what types of games will be in the tournament.
bullets.model_answer: ¡Buenas tardes! ¿Qué tipos de juegos habrá en el torneo?
bullets.note: ¿qué tipos de...? (what types of?) + habrá (future of haber = there will be)

bullets.prompt: Say what type of games you prefer and why.
bullets.model_answer: Prefiero los juegos de aventura porque son más emocionantes que los juegos de deportes.

bullets.prompt: Say how long you have been playing video games.
bullets.model_answer: Juego a videojuegos desde hace cuatro años.
bullets.note: desde hace + present tense (juego, not he jugado)

bullets.prompt: Ask what time the tournament starts and whether there is an entry fee.
bullets.model_answer: ¿A qué hora empieza el torneo y hay que pagar para participar?
bullets.note: ¿a qué hora empieza? + ¿hay que pagar? (do you have to pay?)

gold.correct_text: Juego a videojuegos desde hace tres años y prefiero los juegos en línea porque son más emocionantes.

gold.question: Complete the sentence
sentence_parts: cuánto tiempo pasan jugando para que no

gaps.rule: Present subjunctive — after es importante que
gaps.correct_explain: controlen is the present subjunctive of controlar. After impersonal expressions like es importante que, Spanish requires the subjunctive.

wrong.controlan: controlan is the present indicative. After es importante que, use the present subjunctive: controlen.
wrong.controlar: controlar is the infinitive. After es importante que + subject, use the subjunctive: controlen.

gaps.correct_explain: desarrollen (they develop) is the present subjunctive of desarrollar. After para que (so that), the subjunctive is required.

wrong.desarrollan: desarrollan is the present indicative. After para que, use the present subjunctive: desarrollen.

gold.english: It is important that young people **control** how much time they spend gaming so that they don't **develop** an addiction to video games.
